newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Osprey keen on expanding Gotaas-Larsen links - paper.
newsitem.headline: Osprey keen on expanding Gotaas-Larsen links - paper.

text.p: Osprey Maritime has acknowleged an interest in expanding business links with London-based shipping firm Gotaas-Larsen but refused to say whether it would buy the company for US$500-$800 million, the Straits Times newspaper said on Saturday.
The paper said Osprey director Erling Strom on Friday refused to be drawn on whether his company was engaged in takeover talks with the 50-year-old shipping firm.
The two have a joint operation that owns the 1981-built Golar Spirit, a liquefied natural gas (LNG) carrier.

"We have had discussions with respect to expanding this cooperation...no agreement has been finalised. We will come out with a comment when we can say something. If there is anything to announce, we'll come out with that in the near term," the paper quoted Strom as saying.

Speculation about a deal between the two has been growing for the past two weeks. The Asian Wall Street Journal on Friday quoted unnamed souces as saying that Osprey planned to buy Gotaas-Larsen for US$500-800 million.
Gotaas-Larsen on Friday declined to comment.
